text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Wednesday morning newspapers:
- Sir Arthur Watts, international coordinator of negotiations on the division of assets of former Yugoslavia, said agreement between the ex-Yugoslav states was still far away.
- Spanish state secretary Ramon de Miguel on Tuesday reiterated Spain supported Slovenia's membership in NATO in the first round of NATO's enlargement.
- March pensions will remain unchanged from those in February and January, the Pension Fund said.
- Slovenia's new archbishop Franc Rode said one of his main goals was to determine the legal position of the Catholic Church.
- A five-day sport and tourist fair, Alpe Adria, opened in Ljubljana on Tuesday.
- Slovenia's sole airline Adria Airways said it would buy two Canadair Regional Jets that would replace an Airbus and two Dash 7 planes which will be sold this year.
- Troubled shoe maker Planika said it needed to postpone repayments on its debt totalling $30 million in order to be able to continue with production.

- State Securities Market Agency said investment funds, which participated in the general privatisation process, will be able to apply for a listing on the over-the-counter (OTC) market of the Ljubljana bourse from now on.
- The supervisory board of the city of Maribor said mayor Alojz Krizman may have breached the law by giving guarantees for repayment of a bank loan to the local football club.
